extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (or advanced undergraduates) studying algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding and computing cup-product (ring) structures in cohomology, the external/cross product and Künneth isomorphisms for products and smash products of spaces (especially CW complexes), and applying these to examples (tori, projective spaces, James reduced product) and realization questions for polynomial cohomology algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior algebra for tori and products of odd spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: For the n-torus T^n (and more generally any product of odd-dimensional spheres) H^*(T^n; R) ≈ R[α1, ··· , αn] where this is the exterior algebra with the αi in odd degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: H^*(T^2; Z) ≈ Z[α,β] with |α|=|β|=1. More generally H^*(S^{k1}×···×S^{kn}; Z) ≈ tensor product of one-variable exterior algebras when the ki are all odd (Example 3.16). Use the graded tensor product viewpoint to account for signs/graded-commutativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced homomorphisms preserve ring structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Induced homomorphisms on cohomology (i^* etc.) are ring homomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 3.10 guarantees that maps induced by inclusions or continuous maps commute with cup product; coordinate projections/inclusions give coordinatewise ring homomorphisms used in product and wedge decompositions (Example 3.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product ring isomorphism for products/wedge sums (coordinatewise multiplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cohomology of a product α X_α (or wedge sums, with basepoint hypotheses) decomposes as a product (or appropriate tensor) with respect to coordinatewise multiplication; inclusions induce coordinate functions which are ring homomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Example 3.14 the map H^*(∏ X_α;R) → ∏ H^*(X_α;R) whose coordinates are induced by inclusions is a ring isomorphism (and similarly for wedge sums when basepoints are deformation retracts of neighborhoods). Use this to analyze splittings and detect nontrivial attaching maps (e.g., CP^2 vs S^2∨S^4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cup product can detect nontrivial attaching maps / distinguish homotopy types
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring structure (cup products) can distinguish spaces that have the same additive cohomology but different multiplicative structure (e.g., CP^2 vs S^2 ∨ S^4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additive homology/cohomology alone may not detect that an attaching map is nontrivial; check cup squares and other products (CP^2: H^*(CP^2;Z) ≈ Z[α]/(α^3) so a generator in H^2 has nonzero square, while in S^2∨S^4 each H^2 element squares to 0). Use cup products to rule out wedge-sum decompositions up to homotopy.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Realization Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Which graded commutative R-algebras occur as cup-product algebras H^*(X;R) of spaces X?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difficulty depends on coefficient ring R: over Q essentially every graded commutative Q-algebra is realizable (Quillen 1969); over Z_p (p prime) it's much harder with only partial results; over Z very little is known beyond implications from Z_p cases. Use this as a guiding question for constructing or ruling out cohomology rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and bilinearity of the cross (external cup) product
rubrics_metrics.description: The cross product H^*(X;R) × H^*(Y;R) → H^*(X×Y;R) is defined by a×b = p1^*(a) ∪ p2^*(b) (or as the induced homomorphism via projections), and is bilinear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because cup product is distributive the cross product is linear in each variable. To get an algebra homomorphism one replaces the direct product by the tensor product and uses the graded multiplication rule (a⊗b)(c⊗d)=(-1)^{|b||c|} ac⊗bd to account for signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded multiplication rule in tensor products
rubrics_metrics.description: Define multiplication in a tensor product of graded rings by (a⊗b)(c⊗d) = (−1)^{|b||c|} (ac ⊗ bd), where |x| denotes degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With this sign convention the cross product map µ: H^*(X;R) ⊗_R H^*(Y;R) → H^*(X×Y;R) becomes a ring homomorphism (proof given via projection/pullback identities). Always track degrees when multiplying tensors to include the correct Koszul sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Künneth isomorphism (Theorem 3.15) — sufficient condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The cross product H^*(X;R) ⊗_R H^*(Y;R) → H^*(X×Y;R) is an isomorphism of rings if X and Y are CW complexes and H^k(Y;R) is a finitely generated free R-module for all k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core Künneth-type criterion used to compute cohomology rings of product spaces. The proof is via treating the functors h_n(X)=⊕ H^i(X;R)⊗ H^{n-i}(Y;R) and k_n(X)=H^n(X×Y;R), showing they are cohomology theories and using a natural transformation µ that is an iso on a point then everywhere by Proposition 3.17. Verify CW hypotheses and freeness in computations; failure of freeness can break the isomorphism (see §3.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeness hypothesis caveat for Künneth
rubrics_metrics.description: The freeness (H^k(Y;R) finitely generated free R-module) hypothesis in the Künneth theorem cannot always be dispensed with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are counterexamples when torsion or non-free modules occur; later sections (§3.B) treat general Künneth formulas for homology. Always check module-structure hypotheses before applying the simple tensor-product Künneth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor/torsion algebra facts used in Künneth arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard algebraic properties of tensor products (symmetry, distributivity over direct sums, behavior with Z and finite cyclic groups, and induced maps f⊗g) are prerequisites for the cross-product arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recall: Z⊗A≈A, Z_n⊗A≈A/nA, bilinear maps induce homomorphisms A⊗B→C, and for R-modules impose r a ⊗ b = a ⊗ r b. Use these to manipulate tensor products when checking Künneth hypotheses and computing examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Künneth isomorphism (Theorem 3.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For CW pairs (X,A) and (Y,B), the cross product H^*(X,A;R) ⊗_R H^*(Y,B;R) → H^*(X×Y, A×Y ∪ X×B;R) is an isomorphism of rings if H^k(Y,B;R) is a finitely generated free R-module for each k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductions use collapsing B to a point and split short exact sequences when B is a retract; deduce the general relative case from the absolute case via five-lemma arguments. Use this for cohomology of pairs, smash products, and suspension arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced cross product / smash-product isomorphism and suspension isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The reduced cross product H^*(X;R) ⊗_R H^*(Y;R) → H^*(X ∧ Y;R) is an isomorphism if one factor has finitely generated free cohomology in each degree; e.g., cross product with generator of H^k(S^k;R) gives suspension isomorphisms H^n(X;R) ≈ H^{n+k}(X∧S^k;R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when computing reduced/cohomology of smash products and to derive suspension isomorphisms; example: X∧S^k is the k-fold reduced suspension Σ^k X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial cohomology of projective spaces (Theorem 3.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: H^*(RP^n; Z2) ≈ Z2[α]/(α^{n+1}), H^*(RP^∞; Z2) ≈ Z2[α] with |α|=1. For complex: H^*(CP^n; Z) ≈ Z[α]/(α^{n+1}), H^*(CP^∞; Z) ≈ Z[α] with |α|=2. Quaternionic: H^*(HP^n; Z) ≈ Z[α]/(α^{n+1}) with |α|=4, HP^∞ ≈ Z[α].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved via geometry of projective spaces, excision, deformation retractions, cellular cohomology, and Künneth-type reduction (Example and diagram chase). Use these as canonical examples of polynomial/truncated polynomial cohomology rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using cellular/cofibration/excision arguments to identify multiplicative generators
rubrics_metrics.description: To show cup products of generators produce higher-degree generators (e.g., generator in H^i ∪ generator in H^{n-i} gives generator in H^n for P^n), use deformation retractions, excision, cellular cohomology, and relative Künneth for cubes or disks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The textbook gives a diagrammatic proof reducing to cross product of generators in cubes (I^i × I^j) or spheres; follow diagrams (i) and (ii) and excision/isomorphism steps to push multiplicative statements to relative Künneth computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hopf obstruction via cohomology (Theorem 3.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R^n admits the structure of a division algebra over R, then n must be a power of 2 (proved using induced maps on Z2-cohomology and binomial-type equations in Z2[α1,α2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cohomology ring H^*(RP^{n-1};Z2) and the induced map from multiplication give algebraic constraints ( (α1+α2)^n = 0 ) that force n to be a power of 2. Similar arguments over C show no higher-dimensional division algebras over C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology of James reduced product J(S^n) (Proposition 3.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: J(S^n) has exactly one cell in each dimension a multiple of n, so H^*(J(S^n);Z) consists of Z's in dimensions multiples of n. For n even, cup powers satisfy x1^m = m! x_m (divided polynomial behavior); for n odd different formulae produce polynomial-like structure (H^*(J(S^{2n});Q) ≈ Q[x]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute via quotient maps q:(S^n)^m→J_m(S^n) and cellular cohomology; q^*(x1)=α1+···+αm leads to factorial coefficients in cup powers. For n even the ring identifies with the divided polynomial subring of Q[x] generated by x_i = x^i/i!; for n odd a different combinatorial computation applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraints on realizability of single-generator polynomial rings (table)
rubrics_metrics.description: For which degrees d does there exist X with H^*(X;R) ≈ R[α] with |α|=d? Table: for R=Z: d=2,4; for R=Q: any even d; for R=Z2: d=1,2,4; for R=Z_p (p odd): any even divisor of 2(p−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These constraints come from commutativity and deeper obstructions (e.g., K-theory, Adams-type results); note d must be even unless R=Z2. Exceptional cases (e.g., R=Z2, d=8) require special treatment (Toda). Realizability constructions and obstructions are treated in later sections (§4L, §3.G, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of CW complexes X_d with a single cell in each multiple of d realizing cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: For each admissible even d there exists a CW complex X_d with one cell in each dimension a multiple of d having H^*(X_d; R) ≈ R[α] for the allowed coefficient rings R (constructed in [Hoffman & Porter 1973], [SSAT]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: X_2 = CP^∞, X_4 = HP^∞. For other d the existence uses careful constructions; when verifying realizability aim for minimal CW structures with one cell per multiple of d to match polynomial behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Products and classifying spaces realize many polynomial cohomology rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Products of spaces with polynomial cohomology produce polynomial rings in several variables; furthermore Grassmannians and classifying spaces (G_n(C^∞)=BU(n), G_n(H^∞)=BSp(n), BSU(n)) realize polynomial rings Z[α1,...,αn] with prescribed degrees |α_i|=2i or 4i (or omit α1 for BSU(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use products (and Künneth isomorphism under hypotheses) and known classifying spaces to construct multi-variable polynomial cohomology rings with explicitly known generator degrees. Andersen & Grodal (2008) classify realizable polynomial cup-product rings with Z coefficients using these examples and products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free graded commutative algebra classification (generators and relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A free graded commutative algebra is a tensor product of single-generator free graded commutative algebras, which are either polynomial algebras R[α] on even-degree generators or quotients R[α]/(2α^2) with α odd-degree. Over fields of characteristic ≠2 these quotients are exterior algebras; in characteristic 2 polynomial and exterior collapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every graded commutative algebra is a quotient of such a free one. When attempting to realize or present cohomology rings, express them as tensor products of single-variable building blocks and record whether generators are even or odd degree to determine relations/signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcomplexes of the n-torus realize many nonfree cup-product algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the standard cell structure on T^n with H^*(T^n;Z) ≈ Z[α1,...,αn] (exterior algebra), a subcomplex X ⊂ T^n obtained by omitting certain product cells has H^*(X;Z) equal to the quotient of Z[α1,...,αn] by the ideal generated by the monomials corresponding to omitted minimal cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct explicit examples by deleting cells: e.g., deleting certain 2-cells in T^3 yields H^*(X;Z) ≈ Z[α1,α2,α3]/(α2α3). Use this to build many realizable nonfree cup-product algebras and to analyze which monomials survive in cohomology.
